predecessors.name: Kievan Rus'
predecessors.text: Novgorod, which Yaroslav's division of 1054 gave to Iziaslav I with Kiev (Kievan Rus' page); Cliopatria's first shape of this state is 1056

successors.name: Grand Principality of Moscow
successors.text: the whole Novgorod land as it stood in 1468, annexed by Ivan III in January 1478 ('Novgorod was then formally annexed by Moscow in 1478', Battle of Shelon page)

ledger.x: 1054: Yaroslav's death divides Rus' and Novgorod goes with Kiev to his eldest son.
1126: the Novgorod land reaches the portage and the Dvina side.
1136: Novgorod throws off the princes of Kiev and becomes a republic.
1236: Cliopatria's Novgorod loses the Ladoga-Onega Karelia strip.
September 1240: Izborsk and Pskov fall to the Livonian side.
Winter 1240-1241: the Votic land is overrun.
1241: Alexander Nevsky retakes Pskov.
1241: Votia and the fortress of Koporye are retaken.
1285: Pskov stands apart from Novgorod.
1293: the Swedes take part of western Karelia and found Viborg.
1294: Cliopatria's Novgorod regains the Ladoga-Karelia strip it lacked since 1236.
1300: the Swedes build Landskrona at the mouth of the Neva.
1301: Novgorod destroys Landskrona.
1314: Karelia rises against Novgorod.
1314: the rising is put down after several months.
1314: the Novgorod shape swells over the whole north: Pomorye, Zavolochye, the Pechora and the Urals side, +3,668 cells.
12 August 1323: the Treaty of Nöteborg gives Sweden the border parishes of Savonia.
12 August 1323: eastern Karelia goes to Novgorod under the Treaty of Nöteborg.
1344: Moscow's shape takes cells in the Volga-Mologa south-east of the Novgorod land.
1397: Moscow annexes the Dvina Lands.
1398: Novgorod recovers the Dvina Lands, 'the following year'.
1463: Moscow's shape takes the Vologda side of the Novgorod land.
1468: Cliopatria's Novgorod shape reaches the Kola coast.
23 May 1471: Ivan III goes to war with Novgorod.
14 July 1471: Moscow wins at the Shelon and Novgorod then signs the Treaty of Korostyn.
January 1478: Ivan III annexes Novgorod.
January 1478: the Novgorod Republic ends.

wars.name: Battle on the Ice
wars.outcome: Novgorod-Vladimir victory: Pskov, Votia and Koporye retaken in 1241, the Order beaten on Lake Peipus on 5 April 1242 and, in the settlement, giving up 'the land of the Vod people, of Luga, Pleskov [Pskov], and Lotygola [Latgale]'.

wars.name: Swedish–Novgorodian Wars
wars.outcome: Mixed: Novgorod holds the Neva (Landskrona destroyed 1301), Sweden takes Viborg (1293); the Treaty of Nöteborg (12 August 1323) fixes the frontier; Magnus Eriksson's 1348 crusade burns Oreshek and Novgorod regains control; last recorded conflict 1445.

wars.name: Karelian rising of 1314
wars.outcome: Karelia 'again submitted to Novgorod's authority' after several months.

wars.name: Treaty of Yazhelbitsy
wars.outcome: Novgorod 'sustained a crushing defeat' in 1456 and signed at Yazhelbitsy in February 1456, losing its independent foreign policy and legislation; no territory is named on the page.

wars.name: Battle of Shelon
wars.outcome: Moscow wins at the Shelon on 14 July 1471 (Novgorodians at least 10,000 against 4,000-5,000); the Treaty of Korostyn makes Novgorod 'a patrimony of the grand prince' and bars Lithuanian princes.

wars.name: Annexation of Novgorod by Moscow
wars.outcome: Ivan III marches in the winter of 1477-1478, takes direct control in January 1478 and abolishes the veche; Novgorod is 'formally annexed by Moscow in 1478'.

certainty.note: Forest, lake and portage frontiers never fixed by treaty; the western frontier with the Livonian Order is settled in the peace of 1242 only by naming lands, not a line.

The Swedish frontier on the Karelian Isthmus and in Savonia is regulated by the Treaty of Nöteborg (12 August 1323) and is the one sharper border; the northern colonies (Pomorye, Zavolochye, Pechora, Kola) are soft throughout.
